typedef enum {

  UTF8PROC_STABLE    = (1<<1),
  UTF8PROC_COMPAT    = (1<<2),
  UTF8PROC_COMPOSE   = (1<<3),
  UTF8PROC_DECOMPOSE = (1<<4),
  UTF8PROC_IGNORE    = (1<<5),
  UTF8PROC_REJECTNA  = (1<<6),
  UTF8PROC_NLF2LS    = (1<<7),
  UTF8PROC_NLF2PS    = (1<<8),
  UTF8PROC_NLF2LF    = (UTF8PROC_NLF2LS | UTF8PROC_NLF2PS),
  UTF8PROC_STRIPCC   = (1<<9),
  UTF8PROC_CASEFOLD  = (1<<10),
  UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND = (1<<11),
  UTF8PROC_LUMP      = (1<<12),
  UTF8PROC_STRIPMARK = (1<<13),
  UTF8PROC_STRIPNA    = (1<<14),
} utf8proc_option_t;

functions.name: utf8proc_version
functions.description: Return the utf8proc API version as a string in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format, possibly with a "-dev" suffix for development versions. Intended for runtime checks or logging.

functions.name: utf8proc_unicode_version
functions.description: Return the supported Unicode data version as a string in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. Useful for feature gating or diagnostics.

functions.name: utf8proc_errmsg
functions.description: Return a human-readable error message for a given utf8proc error code (e.g., values returned by processing functions).
requirements: Caller should pass an error code as returned by utf8proc APIs (typically negative constants like UTF8PROC_ERROR_*).
Caller should treat the returned pointer as read-only.

functions.name: utf8proc_iterate
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_iterate(const utf8proc_uint8_t *str, utf8proc_ssize_t strlen, utf8proc_int32_t *codepoint_ref);
functions.description: Decode a single Unicode codepoint from a UTF-8 byte sequence. Reads up to strlen bytes (or up to 4 bytes if strlen < 0). On success writes the decoded codepoint to codepoint_ref and returns the number of bytes consumed; on failure writes -1 to codepoint_ref and returns a negative error code.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to the byte sequence to decode.
codepoint_ref must be a valid, writable pointer.
If strlen >= 0, it must be the maximum number of bytes available from str.
Caller must check the return value: >0 indicates bytes read; <0 indicates an error (see utf8proc_errmsg).

functions.name: utf8proc_codepoint_valid
functions.description: Return 1 if codepoint is within the valid Unicode scalar value range (assigned or unassigned); otherwise 0.

functions.name: utf8proc_encode_char
functions.description: Encode a single Unicode codepoint into UTF-8, writing to dst. Returns the number of bytes written on success, or 0 on failure. This function does not validate that the codepoint is a valid Unicode scalar value.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least 4 bytes.
Caller is responsible for ensuring codepoint is valid if required by the application.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: utf8proc_get_property
functions.description: Look up and return a pointer to a constant struct of Unicode properties for codepoint. For invalid or unassigned codepoints, returns a special struct with category = UTF8PROC_CATEGORY_CN.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned pointer as read-only.

functions.name: utf8proc_decompose_char
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_decompose_char(utf8proc_int32_t codepoint, utf8proc_int32_t *dst, utf8proc_ssize_t bufsize, utf8proc_option_t options, int *last_boundclass);
functions.description: Decompose a single codepoint into a sequence of codepoints according to options (e.g., compatibility decomposition, casefolding, stripping marks, etc.). Optionally inserts 0xFF boundaries if UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND is set. Returns the number of codepoints written on success, or a negative error code. If the required output exceeds bufsize, returns the required size and overwrites dst with undefined data.
requirements: dst must point to a writable array of at least bufsize utf8proc_int32_t elements.

If options includes UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND and processing a stream in order, last_boundclass must be a valid pointer initialized to 0 at the start of the string and preserved between calls; otherwise it may be ignored.
If options includes UTF8PROC_REJECTNA, unassigned codepoints will cause an error.
Caller must check the return value and, if it exceeds bufsize, reallocate and retry (contents are undefined when too small).

functions.name: utf8proc_decompose
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_decompose(const utf8proc_uint8_t *str, utf8proc_ssize_t strlen, utf8proc_int32_t *buffer, utf8proc_ssize_t bufsize, utf8proc_option_t options);
functions.description: Decompose a UTF-8 string into UTF-32 codepoints according to options, with canonical ordering of decomposed sequences. If UTF8PROC_NULLTERM is set, stops at NUL; otherwise processes exactly strlen bytes. Writes results to buffer and returns the number of codepoints written, a negative error code on failure, or the required buffer size if bufsize is too small (in which case buffer contents are undefined).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to the input bytes.
If options includes UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, str must be NUL-terminated; otherwise strlen must specify the number of bytes to process.
buffer must point to a writable array of at least bufsize utf8proc_int32_t elements.
Caller must check the return value and handle negative errors and the resize case (return > bufsize).

functions.name: utf8proc_decompose_custom
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_decompose_custom(const utf8proc_uint8_t *str, utf8proc_ssize_t strlen, utf8proc_int32_t *buffer, utf8proc_ssize_t bufsize, utf8proc_option_t options, utf8proc_custom_func custom_func, void *custom_data);
functions.description: Like utf8proc_decompose, but applies a user-supplied custom_func(codepoint, custom_data) to each codepoint in str before other transformations. Returns the number of codepoints written, a negative error code, or the required buffer size if bufsize is too small. If custom_func is NULL, it is ignored.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer; if UTF8PROC_NULLTERM is set it must be NUL-terminated; otherwise strlen bytes are processed.
buffer must point to a writable array of at least bufsize utf8proc_int32_t elements.
custom_func may be NULL; if non-NULL it must conform to utf8proc_custom_func and be safe for the range of codepoints encountered.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors and the resize case (buffer contents undefined when too small).

functions.name: utf8proc_normalize_utf32
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_normalize_utf32(utf8proc_int32_t *buffer, utf8proc_ssize_t length, utf8proc_option_t options);
functions.description: Normalize a sequence of UTF-32 codepoints in-place according to options (e.g., NLF transformations, control stripping, composition, stability constraints). Returns the resulting length in codepoints on success or a negative error code.
requirements: buffer must point to a writable array of length codepoints.
Each entry in buffer must be within 0x0000..0x10FFFF; otherwise the program might crash (per warning).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: utf8proc_reencode
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_reencode(utf8proc_int32_t *buffer, utf8proc_ssize_t length, utf8proc_option_t options);
functions.description: Re-encode a UTF-32 sequence in-place to UTF-8, optionally normalizing according to options. Returns the length in bytes of the resulting NUL-terminated UTF-8 string on success, or a negative error code.
requirements: buffer must have at least one byte of free space beyond the input data to accommodate the terminating NUL (per warning).
buffer must contain length valid Unicode codepoints in the range 0x0000..0x10FFFF; otherwise the program might crash (per warning).
buffer must be writable.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: utf8proc_grapheme_break_stateful
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_bool utf8proc_grapheme_break_stateful(utf8proc_int32_t codepoint1, utf8proc_int32_t codepoint2, utf8proc_int32_t *state);
functions.description: Return whether a grapheme cluster break is permitted between two consecutive codepoints, implementing UAX#29 extended grapheme cluster rules with state for Unicode 9+ behavior when state is provided.
requirements: If state is non-NULL, the function must be called in order on all potential break positions in the string. It is safe to reset *state to 0 after a detected break.
If state is NULL, rules GB10/12/13 (which require state) are not applied, matching Unicode 8 behavior.

functions.name: utf8proc_grapheme_break
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_bool utf8proc_grapheme_break(utf8proc_int32_t codepoint1, utf8proc_int32_t codepoint2);
functions.description: Return whether a grapheme break is permitted between two consecutive codepoints using the legacy (pre-Unicode 9) algorithm without state. Kept for compatibility.

functions.name: utf8proc_tolower
functions.description: Map a codepoint to its lowercase equivalent if one exists; otherwise return c unchanged (also returns c if c is not a valid codepoint).

functions.name: utf8proc_toupper
functions.description: Map a codepoint to its uppercase equivalent if one exists; otherwise return c unchanged (also returns c if c is not a valid codepoint).

functions.name: utf8proc_totitle
functions.description: Map a codepoint to its titlecase equivalent if one exists; otherwise return c unchanged (also returns c if c is not a valid codepoint).

functions.name: utf8proc_islower
functions.description: Return 1 if the codepoint corresponds to a lowercase character, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: utf8proc_isupper
functions.description: Return 1 if the codepoint corresponds to an uppercase character, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: utf8proc_charwidth
functions.description: Return a display width analogous to wcwidth(codepoint). For non-printable codepoints, returns 0 (unlike wcwidth which returns -1).

functions.name: utf8proc_charwidth_ambiguous
functions.description: Return whether the codepoint has East Asian width class Ambiguous (A). Such characters are considered width 1 if printable, though some East Asian fonts render them double-width.

functions.name: utf8proc_category
functions.description: Return the Unicode general category of the codepoint as a utf8proc_category_t value.

functions.name: utf8proc_category_string
functions.description: Return the two-letter, NUL-terminated Unicode category string for the codepoint (e.g., "Lu", "Co").
requirements: Caller should treat the returned pointer as read-only.

functions.name: utf8proc_map
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_map(const utf8proc_uint8_t *str, utf8proc_ssize_t strlen, utf8proc_uint8_t **dstptr, utf8proc_option_t options);
functions.description: Transform a UTF-8 string according to options (e.g., normalize, casefold, strip marks) and return a newly malloc-allocated UTF-8 string via dstptr. Returns the length of the new string on success or a negative error code on failure. The result is NUL-terminated.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to input bytes.
If options includes UTF8PROC_NULLTERM, str must be NUL-terminated; otherwise strlen specifies the number of bytes to process.
dstptr must be a valid pointer to receive the allocated buffer pointer.
The returned buffer is allocated with malloc and must be freed with free by the caller.
Caller must check the return value for errors before using *dstptr.

functions.name: utf8proc_map_custom
functions.signature: UTF8PROC_DLLEXPORT utf8proc_ssize_t utf8proc_map_custom(const utf8proc_uint8_t *str, utf8proc_ssize_t strlen, utf8proc_uint8_t **dstptr, utf8proc_option_t options, utf8proc_custom_func custom_func, void *custom_data);
functions.description: Like utf8proc_map, but first applies a user-supplied custom_func(codepoint, custom_data) to each codepoint in str before other transformations. Returns the length of the newly malloc-allocated UTF-8 result or a negative error code. The result is NUL-terminated. If custom_func is NULL it is ignored.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer; if UTF8PROC_NULLTERM is set it must be NUL-terminated; otherwise strlen bytes are processed.
dstptr must be a valid pointer to receive the allocated result.
The returned buffer is allocated with malloc and must be freed with free by the caller.
custom_func may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be callable for all codepoints encountered.
Caller must check the return value for errors before using *dstptr.

functions.name: utf8proc_NFD
functions.description: Return a newly allocated NFD-normalized UTF-8 string from the NUL-terminated input str. Shortcut for utf8proc_map(NULLTERM|STABLE|DECOMPOSE).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned buffer is allocated (via malloc) and must be freed with free by the caller.

functions.name: utf8proc_NFC
functions.description: Return a newly allocated NFC-normalized UTF-8 string from the NUL-terminated input str. Shortcut for utf8proc_map(NULLTERM|STABLE|COMPOSE).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned buffer is allocated (via malloc) and must be freed with free by the caller.

functions.name: utf8proc_NFKD
functions.description: Return a newly allocated NFKD-normalized UTF-8 string from the NUL-terminated input str. Shortcut for utf8proc_map(NULLTERM|STABLE|DECOMPOSE|COMPAT).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned buffer is allocated (via malloc) and must be freed with free by the caller.

functions.name: utf8proc_NFKC
functions.description: Return a newly allocated NFKC-normalized UTF-8 string from the NUL-terminated input str. Shortcut for utf8proc_map(NULLTERM|STABLE|COMPOSE|COMPAT).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned buffer is allocated (via malloc) and must be freed with free by the caller.

functions.name: utf8proc_NFKC_Casefold
functions.description: Return a newly allocated NFKC_Casefold normalized UTF-8 string from the NUL-terminated input str. Shortcut for utf8proc_map(NULLTERM|STABLE|COMPOSE|COMPAT|CASEFOLD|IGNORE).
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
Returned buffer is allocated (via malloc) and must be freed with free by the caller.

data_types.description: A byte sequence intended to represent a UTF-8 encoded string. The data may be arbitrary and not necessarily valid UTF-8; functions may interpret it as a NUL-terminated string or process a specified length. Includes possible embedded NULs and malformed sequences.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8 byte sequences tailored to exercise utf8proc routines.
# It focuses on valid, interesting strings with combinations that trigger decomposition,
# composition, casefolding, width, grapheme boundaries, emoji sequences, and embedded NULs.

MAX_LEN = 4096

# Helper: encode a Unicode string to UTF-8 bytes safely

def enc(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('utf-8')

# Building blocks: curated snippets that each exercise specific behavior
SNIPPETS: List[bytes] = []

# ASCII and control
SNIPPETS.append(enc(""))                           # empty
SNIPPETS.append(enc("ASCII"))
SNIPPETS.append(b"A\x00B\x00C")                    # embedded NULs
SNIPPETS.append(bytes(range(1, 32)))                # C0 controls (no NUL)
SNIPPETS.append(b"\t\n\r ")                        # whitespace/newline variants

# Multibyte sequences and boundaries
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u00A9\u20AC\u2603"))         # © € ☃ (2,3,3-byte)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u03B1\u03B2\u03B3"))         # Greek lowercase
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u0410\u0431\u044F"))         # Cyrillic mix

# Decomposition/composition triggers
SNIPPETS.append(enc("A\u0301"))                     # A + COMBINING ACUTE (NFC/NFD diff)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u00C1"))                      # Á precomposed
SNIPPETS.append(enc("e\u0301\u0323"))               # stacking marks
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u212B"))                      # Å Angstrom sign (compatibility)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\uFB01"))                      # ﬁ ligature (compatibility)

# Case mapping edge cases
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u0130\u0131"))                # LATIN CAPITAL I WITH DOT / dotless i
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u00DF"))                      # German sharp s ß
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u03A3\u03C3\u03C2"))         # Greek sigma variants
SNIPPETS.append(enc("İiIı"))                         # mixed dotted/dotless

# Width and East Asian
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u3000\uFF01\uFF10\uFF41"))   # Ideographic space, fullwidth ! 0 a
SNIPPETS.append(enc("中日韓"))                        # CJK (double-width)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("·•‣"))                           # bullets, ambiguous width

# Emoji and grapheme clusters
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\U0001F469\u200D\U0001F467\u200D\U0001F466"))  # family: woman, girl, boy (ZWJ seq)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\U0001F3F3\uFE0F\u200D\U0001F308"))           # rainbow flag
SNIPPETS.append(enc("👍\uFE0F👍🏻👍🏿"))                 # thumbs up + VS16 + skin tones
SNIPPETS.append(enc("🇺🇳🇺🇸"))                          # regional indicators
SNIPPETS.append(enc("क्\r"))                        # Devanagari virama + CR (edge for GB rules)

# Indic conjunct example (consonant + virama + consonant)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("क्ष"))

# Boundary classes: prepend/extend/spacingmark/ZWJ
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\u0600a"))                      # Arabic number sign (PCM) + a
SNIPPETS.append(enc("a\u0308b"))                      # Extend between base letters
SNIPPETS.append(enc("a\u093E"))                      # Devanagari spacing mark
SNIPPETS.append(enc("a\u200D\u0915"))                # ZWJ then Devanagari KA

# Mixed scripts and numbers
SNIPPETS.append(enc("A1Ａ１١١一二三"))                  # ASCII, fullwidth, Arabic-Indic, CJK numerals

# Long combining sequences to stress buffers
SNIPPETS.append(enc("n" + "\u0303" * 16))            # many combining tildes

# Variation selectors
SNIPPETS.append(enc("a\uFE0E a\uFE0F"))               # text vs emoji presentation selectors

# Private-use and high scalars (valid)
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\uE000\uF8FF"))                 # BMP PUA range ends
SNIPPETS.append(enc("\U000F0000\U0010FFFD"))        # Supplementary PUA and max scalar

# Hangul jamo sequences to test LV/LVT
SNIPPETS.append(enc("한"))                           # Hangul jamo forming syllable
SNIPPETS.append(enc("한"))                             # precomposed syllable

# Lines and paragraph separators
SNIPPETS.append(enc("line1\u000Aline2\u000D\u000Aline3\u2028para\u2029end"))

# Specified length vs NUL-terminated behavior
SNIPPETS.append(b"abc\x00defghi")

# Helper to generate a random valid scalar value (excluding surrogate range)

def rand_scalar(r: random.Random) -> int:
    while True:
        cp = r.randrange(0x110000)
        if not (0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF):
            return cp

# Build a random valid UTF-8 string of varied length and codepoints

def random_valid_utf8(r: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII runs, combining marks after bases, emoji, CJK, and random scalars
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    target = r.randint(1, max(1, min(128, max_bytes)))
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target:
        choice = r.randrange(8)
        if choice == 0:
            # ASCII run
            n = r.randint(1, 16)
            ascii_choices = list(range(0x20, 0x7F)) + [0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D]
            s = ''.join(chr(r.choice(ascii_choices)) for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(enc(s))
        elif choice == 1:
            # Base + 1-3 combining marks
            base = r.choice(['A', 'e', 'n', 'o', 'क', '가'])
            ncomb = r.randint(1, 3)
            combs = ['\u0301', '\u0308', '\u0323', '\u0303']
            s = base + ''.join(r.choice(combs) for _ in range(ncomb))
            parts.append(enc(s))
        elif choice == 2:
            # Emoji with optional VS16 and skin tone
            base = r.choice(["👍", "👩", "👨", "❤", "✈"])
            s = base
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                s += "\uFE0F"
            if base in ("👍",) and r.random() < 0.5:
                tone = r.choice([0x1F3FB, 0x1F3FC, 0x1F3FD, 0x1F3FE, 0x1F3FF])
                s += chr(tone)
            parts.append(enc(s))
        elif choice == 3:
            # ZWJ sequence
            seq = r.choice([
                "👩\u200D👩\u200D👧", "👩\u200D👧\u200D👦", "🤝\uFE0F"
            ])
            parts.append(enc(seq))
        elif choice == 4:
            # Regional indicators pair (flag)
            a = r.randrange(0x1F1E6, 0x1F1FF + 1)
            b = r.randrange(0x1F1E6, 0x1F1FF + 1)
            parts.append(chr(a).encode('utf-8') + chr(b).encode('utf-8'))
        elif choice == 5:
            # CJK chunk
            s = ''.join(chr(r.randrange(0x4E00, 0x9FFF + 1)) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)))
            parts.append(enc(s))
        elif choice == 6:
            # Hangul LV/LVT
            parts.append(enc(r.choice(["한", "한"])))
        else:
            # Random valid scalar
            parts.append(chr(rand_scalar(r)).encode('utf-8'))
        if sum(len(p) for p in parts) > max_bytes:
            break
    b = b''.join(parts)
    return b[:max_bytes]

# Compose a final buffer by concatenating a random selection of curated snippets and random-valid data,
# optionally inserting NULs to exercise NULLTERM vs explicit length paths.

def build_buffer(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Decide how many curated snippets to include
    nfix = r.randint(2, 6)
    choices = r.sample(SNIPPETS, k=nfix)
    for sn in choices:
        out += sn
        # Occasionally insert a NUL or CR/LF boundary
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            out += b"\x00"
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            out += b"\r\n"
        if len(out) > MAX_LEN // 2:
            break
    # Add a random-valid segment
    remaining = max(0, MAX_LEN - len(out) - 16)
    if remaining > 0:
        out += random_valid_utf8(r, remaining)
    # Optionally append more combining marks to stress normalization
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        out += enc("\u0301\u0308\u0323")
    # Ensure length limit
    if len(out) > MAX_LEN:
        out = out[:MAX_LEN]
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # With some probability, return a single curated snippet to target specific paths
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        sn = r.choice(SNIPPETS)
        # Maybe surround with ASCII to create mixed context
        prefix = b"" if r.random() < 0.5 else b"start-"
        suffix = b"" if r.random() < 0.5 else b"-end"
        bts = (prefix + sn + suffix)[:MAX_LEN]
        return bts
    # Otherwise, build a richer buffer
    return build_buffer(r)
